title: Forgot to Clock Out? Fix It From the Couch | vitalii.no
description:
How a kiosk-only edit endpoint lets a wrong shift end time be fixed or reverted straight from the TV remote, no laptop and no login required.

GPS-tracked shifts are usually right, but not always — a phone left in a bag, a dead battery, a shift that ran five minutes over what the tracker caught. Before this, fixing a wrong end time meant opening the admin panel on a laptop; on the TV kiosk, where the family actually reads the work report, there was no way to touch it at all.

I added a kioskEdit() function in workers/youtube-gate/work.js that only ever touches a shift's end time — the start always stays fixed. Passing a manual HH:MM time stores it while keeping the original GPS end time as a fallback, so it can be reverted later. Passing nothing clears the manual edit and hands the day back to GPS automatically. A new POST /work-edit endpoint exposes this with no login, matching the kiosk's existing no-session design, and rejects any date in the future or older than 62 days. On the TV, the work report screen grew an edit button next to each shift's end time, plus a revert option that shows the original GPS time.

Five new unit tests cover the manual edit, the GPS revert, and all four rejected cases — future date, too old, missing row, end before start. Any of the last 62 days can now be corrected straight from the couch.
